top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
top_sast_rules.description: Client-side URL redirection based on unvalidated user input may cause redirection to malicious web sites.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Detect output operations that lack proper encoding for the target context
top_sast_rules.remediation: Validate redirect URLs against allowlists. Use relative URLs where possible and avoid user-controlled redirects.

top_sast_rules.description: Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement strict input validation using allowlists and reject invalid input rather than attempting to sanitize it.

top_sast_rules.description: Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find state-changing operations that lack CSRF protection mechanisms
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookie attributes and validate the Origin/Referer headers.

top_sast_rules.description: Security-critical data assumed immutable can be modified by an attacker.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-471 assumed-immutable immutable-data hidden-field cookie reverse-dns attacker-modified trusted-value mutable security-decision
top_sast_rules.remediation: Do not trust client-modifiable values as immutable security state.
